detailed_records.patient_note: 58-year-old male with sickle cell disease (SCD), avascular necrosis (humeral/femoral), pulmonary hypertension with right heart failure, chronic kidney disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism history presented with chest pain and shortness of breath, diagnosed with sickle cell pain crisis. Chest X-ray showed pulmonary interstitial prominence (congestion/mild edema). Electrocardiogram revealed sinus tachycardia. Hemoglobin decreased to 5.8 g/dL, requiring three packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusions. Pain uncontrolled with morphine patient-controlled analgesia. Subsequent deterioration: diaphoresis, tachycardia, tachypnea, increased oxygen requirement to 15 L/min, intubated, transferred to ICU. Diagnosed with acute chest syndrome (fever, chest pain, bilateral patchy consolidations on chest X-ray). Developed supraventricular tachycardia/atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (>160 bpm) and hypotension; treated with intravenous amiodarone (150 mg bolus, then 1 mg/min drip), later transitioned to oral amiodarone (400 mg twice daily for 10-gram load, then 200 mg daily). Hemoglobin improved from 6.4 g/dL to 9.4 g/dL (hematocrit 19.3% to 28.5%) over four days with one additional pRBC unit, correlating with symptom improvement. Discharged two days after improvement. Continued amiodarone for three months, then discontinued due to long-term side effect concerns; planned ablation.

detailed_records.patient_note: 27-year-old woman with HbSC sickle cell disease and migraine history presented with intractable headaches. Symptoms began 12 days post-Pfizer COVID-19 vaccination (headaches, chills, SOB, left arm swelling; other symptoms resolved except headache). Neurology ruled out SAH via LP (elevated CSF opening pressure 31 cm); MRI brain showed bilateral frontal/parietal subcortical T2 hyperintensities consistent with migraine; MRA/MRV negative. Status migrainosus treated unsuccessfully with prednisone (60 mg x 5 days), valproate, amitriptyline, topiramate, acetazolamide. On day 3, developed neck/shoulder pain (vaso-occlusive crisis) after prednisone; cervical spine MRI negative. Day 5: sphenopalatine block ineffective. Day 6: hematology recommended ketorolac (30 mg IV q8h) and prednisone discontinuation; transfusions not indicated for uncomplicated pain crisis. Day 7: pain progressed, tachypnea (RR 30), acute hypoxic respiratory failure (type 1), transferred to ICU. Lab: Hb 11.8→6.6 g/dL, platelets 238 K/uL→35 K/uL over 4 days, LDH 172→>1800 U/L, AST 9→118 U/L, ALP 64→288 U/L, bilirubin 0.8→1.4 mg/dL, ammonia 46 mmol/L (mild, not explaining altered mentation). Amitriptyline/valproate discontinued; AST/ALP improved (AST 41 U/L, ALP 87 U/L). Day 10: PT elevated (18.8 sec). CT brain showed subtle right corona radiata/basal ganglia hypoattenuation; MRI brain revealed interval microhemorrhages (innumerable small foci of low signal intensity) consistent with fat embolism syndrome (FES) as cause of respiratory failure/ACS. Day 15: received 5 units packed RBCs; HbA 74%. Hemolytic parameters improved. Mentation improved (alert and oriented to time, place, person). Discharged home. Residual numb chin syndrome noted on follow-up.
